sourceRefs.locator: In The Fortified Viking Age, pp. 78–80, fig. 5 and tables 1–2. Riverbank lane before 720, plots 6–8 m wide, Rhineland barrels reused in wells, sequence of individual coin finds and the predominance of Series X from about 725.

European Journal of Archaeology 18, pp. 497–523. The reassessment of the 1985–86 excavations at Sct Nicolajgade 8 uses domestic activity and building remains to propose early permanent occupation on part of the market site.

Archaeological and Anthropological Sciences 14, article 180. Site and materials, table 1 and figs. 1b, 7–8. ASR 9 Post Office site (55°19′44.7″N, 8°46′08.7″E). Early workshop c. 700–720, later workshop c. 760–790. White from bubbles in remelted gold-leaf backing glass and evidence for adding colourants on site.
Fig. 1b and “Site and materials”: Post Office ASR 9 and nearby Posthustorvet excavation. Rounded general marketplace point.
